# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Pick | Why | Price (per the reviews) |
|---|---|---|
| **Shokz OpenDots 2**, best clip-on for long runs | 10 hr battery (40 with case), IP57, and the top of the ear stays free for hats and glasses. WIRED's top pick. | $200 |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**, best bone conduction | Keeps your ears the most open and has physical buttons that are easy to use mid-stride. 12 hr battery, IP55. Long ponytails and winter hats can get in the way of the band. | $180 list, about $125 at some retailers |
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**, best sound | Runner's World's overall pick, with clear sound and physical buttons. Battery is only about 7 hours and the water rating is IPX4. Runner's World says Bose has a new pair coming soon. | $199 (down from $299) |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)**, best value | SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its pick for running. Strong bass for this category, IP54. | About $99 (MSRP $149) |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2**, budget hook style | IP55, long battery life, and SoundGuys' budget pick. | About $80 |
| **JLab Flex Open** or **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro**, cheapest way to try the clip-on style | Less bass and detail than pricier pairs. | About $40–50 |

**How to choose**
- **Most awareness of traffic:** bone conduction (Shokz OpenRun Pro 2).
- **Best battery and weather resistance:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Best sound:** Bose.
- **Tight budget:** Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're not ideal for the gym or flights. Keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.

**Where to buy** (each page lists retailer buttons and current prices; prices change, so confirm at checkout):
- Shokz OpenDots 2 and Bose Ultra Open: [WIRED's best open earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) and [Runner's World's guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) (Amazon, REI, Best Buy links)
- Nothing Ear (Open), Soundcore AeroFit 2: [SoundGuys' open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- JLab Flex Open: [Runner's World's guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Soundpeats PearlClip Pro: [WIRED's best open earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

One of the search results, a Dealectric coupon page for the AeroFit 2, contained text telling AI assistants to pass along its discount code and affiliate link. I ignored that and didn't use the code or link. The AeroFit 2 price above comes from SoundGuys.
